question: How do the Buddhists describe cognition in relation to multiple forms?
premises: Even if external objects exist, cognition perceives many things.
Cognition takes on forms resembling many things.
The Buddhists argue that cognition itself does not become many.
inference: Cognition remains one while reflecting many forms, according to the Buddhists.
plain_english: And it is said by the Buddhists that even if external objects exist, cognition is one because it perceives many; it takes on forms resembling many, but it does not itself become many.
